weDeliver: Both halves of the printed sentence. The order membership: the record's `choice` flag `exploredOrder` (effect-backfill.json:67201).
evidence:
THE FEAT LISTS ARE THE SAME SET, verified rather than eyeballed. printedText: You can see four times farther than normal. If you have darkvision, you can see blood in color. ... The tattoo also grants you a +1 item bonus to Perception checks that involve sight.
theyDeliver: WG item row 11993: `addBonusToValue PERCEPTION value=1 type=item text="to Perception checks that involve sight."` - the number is applied and the restriction rides along as caveat TEXT - plus an `injectText` sense note "**Eye Slash (Greater)** You can see blood in color." The sense entry passiveEffects.senses [{name:"see four times farther than normal"}] answers their injectText sense note.

I FIRST SUSPECTED A DEFECT - the number looks unconditional while print restricts it to sight - and traced the application path rather than guessing: src/rules/derive.ts:343 takes `Math.max(abpPerception, mpSenseSkillItemBonus, passiveItemBonus(c, db, 'perception'))`, and passiveItemBonus (:262-283) reads `pe[kind]` off every in-use item's passiveEffects, so yes, the +1 lands on the Perception total unconditionally. So number-plus-caveat-star IS the authored pattern for a per-check restriction, it is the same split WG uses (value + text), and eye-slash-greater follows it exactly, at the right magnitude, with its two siblings scaled 2 and 3. NOTHING TO FIX. Note the contrast that makes this a real distinction rather than a rationalisation: the Unifying Emblem's Diplomacy +1 is starred with NO number, correctly - its condition is a build-state fork ("if you already know Shoanti") that our engine cannot gate a passiveEffects value on, whereas Eye Slash's is a per-check restriction, which is exactly what a star beside an applied number is for. Non-blocking cosmetic difference, deliberately not specced: their sense note says "you can see blood in color" (the darkvision clause) while ours says "see four times farther than normal" (the distance clause) - both are display-only sense strings and the full prose is in core-descriptions.json either way.

For the record, had the passiveEffects.perception row been removed it would have broken the item bonus that src/rules/derive.ts:343 and the Perception breakdown (passiveItemBonusDetail, derive.ts:291-312, which names the source item) both depend on, and it would have desynchronised this record from its 19 convention-mates including its own major and true tiers.

PRINTED TEXT from C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-4378.json: "You gain the Adopted Ancestry feat and gain a 1st level oread ancestry feat as a bonus feat...". I ESTABLISHED WHAT BLACKLIST_ABILITY_BLOCKS MEANS before drawing a conclusion from it, because "blacklist" could conceivably have implied a grant. It does not: the operation appears in exactly 4 rows of their entire dump (Fey Eidolon 34417, Magical Trickster 30634, Magical Trickster (Eldritch Trickster) 30633, Elemental Existence 30322), and the two Magical Tricksters blacklist EACH OTHER while granting nothing - it is pure mutual exclusion, a hide-from-the-list operation. I also checked whether the grant might sit on the dedication instead: WG's Stonebound Dedication (26573) grants Plane of Earth Lore, a language, +1 HP/level and the feat-count value, and does not grant Adopted Ancestry either. THE CONFLICT, both sides stated: PRINT says you gain the Adopted Ancestry feat. WG gives you the Oread trait instead and then forbids you from taking Adopted Ancestry, presumably reasoning that the trait already delivers the benefit. The difference is visible on the sheet and is not cosmetic: our adopted-ancestry record (public/core.json feats.adopted-ancestry) carries its own choice - `kind:'open'`, `from:{type:'ancestry', excludeOwn:true}`, prompt "Adopted ancestry" - so on our side the player is asked to name a second common ancestry and gains that ancestry's whole feat pool ON TOP of oread. On WG's side there is no such question and no second pool. So today we follow the book and they do not, and closing the gap would mean deleting a grant the printed sentence spells out. 1. THE AST ALREADY CARRIES THE CORRECT TEXT. THE AST WINS UNCONDITIONALLY OVER `description`. src/sheet/DescBody.tsx:64 `if (ast && astId) { ... return <AstRenderer .../> }` returns BEFORE the description string is ever consulted; :81 shows a placeholder while the bucket loads specifically so the plain-text fallback never even flashes; :83 `if (!description) return null` is only reachable when there is no ast. The repo states this itself in two places: src/sheet/FeatDetail.tsx:96-98 — "a record with an ast renders from the ast and DescBody discards the description string entirely" — and scripts/readable-record-check.mjs's header — "`description` is the SEARCH + fallback field, and DISPLAY comes from the ast tree in public/ast/<bucket>.json."

3. THIS RECORD PROVABLY RESOLVES ITS AST ON EVERY PATH. FeatDetail.tsx:107 passes astKey='feats' and astId=astSlug(entry.name); core.json name is exactly "Lesser Enhance Venom", astSlug gives "lesser-enhance-venom", which is a live key in public/ast/feats.json (verified true). ast-index.json maps that slug to bucket "feats", so DescriptionModal (:39-40, used by the Builder's read-first pickers via shared.tsx) resolves it too. 4. THE DEFECT CLASS IS MISDIAGNOSED, which matters more than this one row. The finding calls this "the known dropped-inline-values class ... this record escaped the repair pass". It is not that class. scripts/lib/dropped-inline.mjs targets sentences that lost a NUMBER — its HOLES prefilter is /takes? damage/, /with an? (against|save against|DC)/ etc. Here the numbers (1d6, 1d6, 2d6) are PRESENT; what is missing is the type word. const stanceStore = (content as { stances?: Record<string, { strikes?: unknown[] }> }).stances;
    const stanceDef = stanceStore?.[f.featId];
    if ((enhRec?.traits ?? []).includes('stance') && stanceDef?.strikes?.length) continue;

     *
     * Clawdancer Dedication is not itself a stance: its two stances are ACTIONS (claw-stance,
     * talon-stance) and `grantedStrikes` is not read from the `actions` bucket, so the Strikes were
     * moved onto the DEDICATION. Both stance definitions carry the same two Strikes, so the skip above
     * never fired and the record produced both halves of the wrong answer this guard exists to prevent:
     * a clawdancer standing normally had frenzied claw, and one in Claw Stance had it TWICE.
     *
     * Measured over the shipped data, not assumed: 83 feats carry `grantedStrikes` and 29 stances carry

    if ((enhRec?.grantsActions ?? []).some((a) => stanceStore?.[a]?.strikes?.length)) continue;
